principle: Claims are broken into individually-rated propositions rather than adjudicated as bundles. This matters because the two commonest failures in this material run in opposite directions: treating a source's error on one point as disproof of everything else they said, and treating one authenticated detail as corroboration of an entire narrative. Both are avoided by rating each proposition on its own evidence.

verified.label: Verified
verified.desc: Established by primary source or direct demonstration.

supported.label: Supported
supported.desc: Good evidence, short of direct proof.

documented_allegation.label: Documented allegation
documented_allegation.desc: The claim was definitely made; its truth is a separate question.

counterevidence.label: Counterevidence exists
counterevidence.desc: Affirmative evidence points the other way.

disputes.title: The Fort Huachuca sighting and the Kolvet 'alibi' photograph
disputes.summary: Mitch Snow alleged he was at Fort Huachuca — the U.S. Army installation near Sierra Vista, Arizona — on September 8–9, 2025, and believed he saw Erika Kirk at the Candlewood Suites on the evening of September 8, with a separate claimed sighting involving Brian Harpole around September 9. YouTuber Gary Melton (Paramount Tactical) investigated Snow and became one of his strongest critics. During a livestream, Melton read and displayed messages he said came from Andrew Kolvet / TPUSA, including a photograph presented as 'Proof she was with her kids at 8:33am PT.' Melton immediately realized he had shown material apparently not intended for release and apologized on air — the transcript preserves him saying so.

core_problems.title: The date does not answer the allegation
core_problems.body: Snow's significant Erika allegation concerns the EVENING OF SEPTEMBER 8. The photograph Melton displayed was dated SEPTEMBER 9, 8:33 a.m. Even if the photograph were fully authentic, correctly timestamped, and actually showed Erika with her children, it would not constitute an alibi for the evening of September 8. At most it addresses the following morning. Melton subsequently acknowledged making a date mistake during the livestream.

core_problems.title: Erika apparently is not in the photograph
core_problems.body: The photograph apparently depicts children rather than Erika visibly accompanying them. A photo of someone's children at a location does not establish the parent's location. Innocent scenarios abound: a nanny, relative, Charlie, or another caregiver took it; an older photo was forwarded; someone sent Erika a picture of the children. Establishing her presence would require the original file with EXIF, the original device, a Live Photo sequence, GPS metadata, adjacent photographs, cloud upload records, or another person visibly photographed with her.

core_problems.title: One of the children apparently was not hers
core_problems.body: Melton was challenged because a boy in the photograph appeared substantially older and larger than Erika and Charlie's son, who was reportedly about 16 months old at the time. Melton eventually responded publicly: 'It's not her son, it's her daughter with another child.' That does not make the photograph fake — but it means the original description, 'proof she was with her kids,' was not literally accurate. The claim degraded from 'Erika + her kids' to 'allegedly Erika's daughter + an unrelated child, with Erika not visible.'

core_problems.title: What was called 'metadata' was not forensic metadata
core_problems.body: Melton said he would show the image 'with the metadata' and then pointed to a displayed date and time. There is a vast difference between STRONG forensic metadata — an original JPEG/HEIC containing DateTimeOriginal, camera model, GPS, editing history, device information, timezone, pixel dimensions, an Apple Live Photo companion file, cloud provenance and hashes — and WEAK displayed metadata, which is a screenshot of a phone's Photos screen. The latter can be produced from a file whose creation date changed, or a forwarded, exported or manually altered image. A date displayed on someone's phone is not forensic proof of when the underlying scene occurred.

core_problems.title: The 'AI-generated hand' is not established
core_problems.body: A strange-looking hand is a classic potential AI indicator — and also a classic false positive. Children's hands in compressed photographs can look bizarre due to motion blur, JPEG compression, phone computational photography, HDR frame merging, depth-of-field blur, overlapping fingers, wide-angle distortion or social-media rescaling. Modern AI generators also no longer reliably produce the stereotypical six-finger errors. No original high-resolution copy with sufficient provenance was obtained, so no meaningful forensic examination was possible. Verdict: image deserves forensic examination; AI generation UNPROVEN.

core_problems.title: The 'at the office all day' detail is imprecise
core_problems.body: The message attributed to Kolvet said Erika was 'at the office with Charlie all day.' Subsequent descriptions of Charlie's September 9 schedule and Erika's own recollections do not obviously establish that they spent the entire workday together. That does not establish Kolvet lied — it may be shorthand, mistaken recollection, or information relayed from someone else. But for something offered as an alibi, precision matters enormously. The original complete message thread is needed rather than fragments read aloud.

disputes.separate_question: There is a question here entirely separate from where Erika was: WHY WAS A SENIOR TPUSA COMMUNICATIONS FIGURE PRIVATELY SUPPLYING PURPORTED ALIBI MATERIAL TO A YOUTUBER? That is not inherently improper — an organization facing an explosive accusation would naturally provide evidence privately to people attempting to verify it. But it becomes worth documenting because Melton was simultaneously conducting a very aggressive public effort to discredit Snow. The chain is: Snow alleges → Kolvet/TPUSA privately supplies material → Melton both publishes the 'alibi' and attacks Snow.
disputes.snow_credibility: There is substantial counterevidence concerning Snow. Brian Harpole has sued Candace Owens and Snow for defamation; the complaint reportedly alleges Harpole's airline records place him elsewhere when Snow claimed to see him at Fort Huachuca. That could seriously undermine Snow's Harpole identification. But logically, Snow falsely identifying Harpole does not automatically establish that he falsely identified Erika. Each sighting must be evaluated independently. Similarly, allegations about Snow's criminal or family history affect credibility but do not themselves establish where Erika was on September 8. The strongest rebuttal would be objective contemporaneous evidence placing Erika elsewhere — which has not been publicly produced.

propositions.note: Though this does not validate his identifications.

propositions.note: Transcript preserves his on-air apology to Kolvet.

propositions.note: Verified as what was displayed.

propositions.claim: That timestamp proves when the photograph was taken
propositions.note: Not established without the original file.

propositions.claim: The photo answers the September 8 Erika sighting
propositions.note: Wrong date — it addresses September 9.

propositions.claim: Erika herself appears in the photograph
propositions.note: Apparently not.

propositions.claim: Both children in the photo were Erika's
propositions.note: Melton later said one was not her son.

propositions.note: Classic false-positive indicator.

disputes.bottom_line: The biggest anomaly is not the hand. It is much simpler: the principal allegation concerns September 8, Kolvet supplied something dated September 9, Erika apparently is not visible, one of the supposed 'kids' turns out not to be her son, and what was called metadata has not been demonstrated as original-file forensic metadata. None of that proves Erika went to Fort Huachuca, and it certainly does not prove involvement in the assassination. But the photograph cannot be accepted as a meaningful alibi on the evidence currently available.

disputes.title: Did Gary Melton's position change — and was he influenced?
disputes.summary: Nate Cornacchia (Valhalla VFT), a retired Green Beret from 1st Special Forces Group, has claimed that Gary Melton originally doubted the official story and is now being influenced to align with TPUSA / Erika Kirk / FBI positions. Nate says he knew Melton on an almost personal level. Both men's Special Forces backgrounds are genuine: material predating the Kirk case identifies Melton as a former 1st Special Forces Group Green Beret, sniper-team leader and veteran of four combat deployments.

trajectory.title: The documented position change
steps: Melton's early channel material treated the shooting as an unresolved forensic problem — titles include 'The Charlie Kirk Murder, Conspiracy Theories and What The Evidence Says' and 'Charlie Kirk's Autopsy Timeline: Is It A Cover Up?' He was willing to entertain alternative ballistic and operational possibilities.
He developed a private communication channel with Andrew Kolvet, receiving nonpublic Erika-related rebuttal material — directly demonstrated by the Fort Huachuca livestream incident.

On December 15 he appeared on The Charlie Kirk Show itself, in an episode structured around why Tyler Robinson was the shooter and 'debunking misconceptions.' Hosts described him as having traveled to UVU and retraced Robinson's alleged route.
By July 2026, Jeremy Boreing's show promoted him as someone who had spent nine months 'systematically fact-checking Candace Owens' specific claims against the assassination evidence, one by one.'
His rhetoric became visibly harsher — appearing in programming portraying competing narratives as an 'empire of lies,' and posting openly adversarial content about Nate/Valhalla VFT.

disputes.access_mechanism: The plausible influence mechanism does not require bribery or coercion. A commentator with exclusive access faces a familiar incentive loop: access → exclusive information → audience value → more access. Melton demonstrably received direct responses from Kolvet, unreleased photographs, a TPUSA media appearance, access to Charlie's surviving media staff, and the opportunity to reconstruct UVU evidence. Maintaining that relationship would carry tangible professional value without anyone ever saying 'say this or we cut you off.' This is a real conflict-of-interest issue — he was publicly evaluating allegations about TPUSA and Erika while privately receiving TPUSA's rebuttal material. If that relationship was not transparently disclosed at the outset of his coverage, it is reasonable to ask whether access influenced analysis. But this is an INFERENCE, not proof, and 'he genuinely changed his view after reviewing more evidence' remains equally plausible.
disputes.nuance: One thing weakens a simplistic 'Gary flipped immediately' narrative: Nate initially DEFENDED Gary after Gary had already begun appearing with TPUSA personnel. A contemporaneous comment in the Green Beret community describes Nate defending Gary despite their disagreement over the caliber, and specifically mentions Gary receiving criticism for appearing with Kolvet. The likelier trajectory: both investigated independently → Gary began cooperating with TPUSA → Nate gave him the benefit of the doubt → interpretations diverged → Gary became hostile toward alternative theories → Nate concluded Gary had changed → relationship ruptured. The Mitch Snow / Fort Huachuca episode appears to have been the major fracture point.

propositions.claim: TPUSA paid Gary to change his position
propositions.note: Searched for consulting fees, travel reimbursement, appearance fees, sponsorships, contracts and direct payments. No public record found. This does not establish he was uncompensated — appearance fees and contractor invoices need not be individually public.

propositions.note: The demonstrated chain is Erika-related information → Kolvet → Gary, not Erika → Gary. Do not collapse those propositions absent a message saying so.

propositions.note: Searched for FBI consulting, contracts, private briefings, restricted evidence, payments, and admissions of federal contact. Nothing found. He does have a background including years of tactical instruction for federal personnel — having federal customers is fundamentally different from taking FBI direction.

Gary genuinely changed his view after reviewing more evidence

disputes.bottom_line: There is enough evidence to take Nate's observation seriously, but not enough to accept the full 'Gary was gotten to' allegation as fact. The strongest non-speculative version: Gary started as a relatively independent former-SOF commentator willing to investigate alternative explanations, developed private access to Kolvet/TPUSA, received nonpublic rebuttal material, appeared on TPUSA's own media operation, increasingly defended the prosecution account, and entered an acrimonious feud with a fellow former Green Beret who had earlier defended him. That is real. What cannot be determined is whether the cause was better evidence, loyalty, access, reputational incentives, money, or some combination.
disputes.next_step: A date-by-date position-change timeline: every Kirk-related Melton video and post from September 10 forward, coded for what he believed about the shooter, caliber, wound, security, FBI, TPUSA, Erika, Fort Huachuca and Snow. Overlay the dates of his first private Kolvet contact, first TPUSA appearance, UVU trip, and falling-out with Nate. If positions change sharply immediately after particular contacts, that would be substantially more testable than anything currently available.

disputes.title: 'Uncompressed' comparison images — second suspect / Twiggs in the escape footage
disputes.summary: A set of images circulating online (shown to this app directly, not sourced from CharlieFiles.com) purports to show that Candace Owens released 'uncompressed' versions of the official surveillance stills, and that a proper look at them reveals either a different person than the compressed prosecution images show, or a second figure — identified in this thread as Lance Twiggs, Robinson's former roommate — present in the escape imagery. The comparison set includes: the hooded/backpack stairwell figure in both a standard and a blue-tinted 'enhanced' version; a person in a maroon t-shirt and cap in a parking garage and convenience store, compared to a personal reference photo of a young man in a matching shirt; Tyler Robinson's actual jail booking photos (front and profile); a separate reference photo said to depict Twiggs, outdoors against a brick wall; and a shoe-style comparison between the stairwell figure and a person wearing a cat-ear hat holding a rainbow sign.

core_problems.title: The 'uncompressed' claim is not demonstrated by what was shown
core_problems.body: The blue-tinted version of the stairwell image is a color/contrast filter applied on top of the same low-resolution still — not recovered resolution. A color filter does not add real detail back into an image; it can make a still LOOK more legible without changing the underlying pixel information. Separately, one of the images shown includes a visible webcam inset of a livestreamer, indicating it is a screenshot taken of a YouTube stream — which adds a full additional generation of video compression on top of whatever the platform already re-encoded. That is the opposite of 'uncompressed.' No original file with metadata was produced for any image in this set.

core_problems.title: The image sets do not share a common scene, angle, or clothing
core_problems.body: The hooded stairwell figure, the maroon-shirt garage/store figure, and the Twiggs reference photo are three different settings with three different outfits. A meaningful visual comparison requires either the same moment captured differently (e.g., a compressed vs. uncompressed export of the identical frame) or a controlled comparison method (gait, proportions, fixed reference points) — not three unrelated photos laid side by side. The hood in the stairwell image covers all hair, making any hair-based comparison to the Twiggs reference photo impossible from that image alone.

core_problems.title: Shoe-style matching is circumstantial, not confirmatory
core_problems.body: One comparison circles a similar sneaker style between the stairwell figure and a person in a cat-ear hat holding a rainbow sign. Matching a shoe model between two low-resolution images is a legitimate OSINT starting point, but it identifies a product, not a person — a popular sneaker style is worn by many people. At the resolution shown, even the specific model could not be confirmed as identical, only broadly similar (light-colored sneakers).

core_problems.title: The premise that facial clarity is needed for identification doesn't match the actual state's methodology
core_problems.body: The prosecution's own case agent, David Hull, conceded under testimony that 'the video of the person on the roof, as a standalone, was not distinguishable' — no facial identification was ever claimed from the rooftop footage. The identification actually used gait analysis (a documented 'stiff-right-leg gait' tracked across hundreds of hours of multi-camera footage, absent during the rooftop run itself, attributed to adrenaline), footwear consistency, and a documented clothing change in a stairwell (shirt/shorts to dark pants and a long sleeve with an American-flag graphic), corroborated by DNA, the recovered rifle, and vehicle/plate evidence. A demonstration that a compressed public image doesn't show a clear face does not undermine an identification method that was never claimed to rest on a clear face.

core_problems.title: Perceived height and build across different cameras is not a reliable comparison without a fixed scale reference
core_problems.body: A separate claim raised in this thread is that the person in less-compressed images 'looks taller and bigger overall' than Robinson. Apparent height and bulk in security stills are heavily distorted by camera mounting height, lens angle, distance from the camera, and clothing bulk (a jacket plus backpack materially increases apparent mass). Two different cameras at two different distances will make the same person look different sizes. A reliable comparison requires a shared, fixed reference object (a doorframe, handrail, floor tile, or the subject's own booking-sheet height used as a scale) present in both frames — none was provided here.

core_problems.title: Familiar recognition (family) is not the same evidentiary category as anonymous facial matching from pixels
core_problems.body: A related argument holds that Robinson's family recognizing him from footage, or Robinson himself knowing to surrender, implies the footage must be facially clear enough for a stranger to independently verify. Neither inference holds. People who know someone well can recognize gait, build, posture, and clothing far more reliably than an outside observer matching an unfamiliar face in a degraded still — that is a different and more reliable recognition channel, not evidence the image itself is facially resolvable. Separately, the Discord/text evidence shows Robinson's own decision to surrender is attributed to already knowing what he had done and watching police close in on his rifle's hiding location, not to recognizing his own image in broadcast footage — see the propositions below.

core_problems.title: A newer, more specific claim (post-hearing) needs its own accounting: 'horizontally compressed' court footage versus 'uncompressed' images of a 'maroon boy' in a parking garage
core_problems.body: Distinct from the earlier items in this set, Candace Owens has separately claimed (Episode 374 of her show, ~August 2026) that court-shown surveillance footage was horizontally compressed in a way that made the person appear thinner, and that 'uncompressed' stills she obtained show a stockier build, plus a detail about left-handed phone use. This is a materially different claim from the others in this dispute: aspect-ratio and pixel-format distortion is a real, documented video phenomenon and is not inherently implausible the way shape-matching or filtered-color claims are. Checked against this app's own full preliminary-hearing transcript (all five days, 186,789 words, searched directly): zero occurrences of 'aspect ratio,' 'stretch,' 'squeeze,' 'anamorphic,' or 'pixel' in any relevant context. Agent Hull's actual testimony describes the parking garage sequence and states that the only difference between the enhanced compilation (exhibit 12.1) and the clean version (12.4) in that footage was that individuals' faces were blurred — no mention of zooming, stretching or resizing in that segment specifically. IMPORTANT TIMING CORRECTION: this app initially treated the defence's silence on this specific claim during the hearing as meaningful evidence against it. That inference was wrong and has been withdrawn. The preliminary hearing concluded in July 2026; Owens's 'uncompressed' images were not released until after it ended. The defence could not have addressed a claim that did not yet exist or was not yet public. The claim is therefore genuinely untested by the adversarial process, not tested and rejected by it, and should be rated accordingly rather than folded into the same 'unproven' bucket as the earlier, weaker items in this set.

propositions.claim: Screenshotting a livestream produces 'uncompressed' footage

propositions.note: The state's own case agent, David Hull, testified the standalone rooftop video 'was not distinguishable.' No facial ID was ever the state's claim.

propositions.claim: Therefore, the state's identification of Robinson has no basis
propositions.note: The state's identification methodology rests on gait, footwear, and clothing-change tracking across multi-camera footage, corroborated by DNA, the recovered rifle, and vehicle/plate evidence — not facial clarity.

propositions.claim: The person in comparison images looks taller/bigger than Robinson
propositions.note: No shared, fixed scale reference exists across the compared images; apparent size varies with camera distance, mounting height, and clothing bulk.

propositions.claim: Robinson recognizing himself in broadcast footage explains his decision to surrender
propositions.note: Discord messages beginning Sept 11 7:57 PM show he was already aware of what he had done and was tracking police presence near his hidden rifle's location before surrendering roughly an hour later — not reacting to recognizing his own image.

propositions.claim: Family recognizing Robinson implies the surveillance footage is facially clear
propositions.note: Recognition by people who know a person's gait, build, and mannerisms is a different and more reliable channel than a stranger matching an unfamiliar face in a degraded still.

propositions.claim: Court-shown footage was horizontally compressed and 'uncompressed' images show Robinson's build differently
propositions.note: Technically plausible in principle (aspect-ratio/pixel-format distortion is real), but no original file or metadata has been produced for the 'uncompressed' images, no shared scene or fixed scale reference exists to compare build across two different photographs, and the claim postdates the preliminary hearing entirely so it has not been tested by cross-examination. This app initially argued the defence's silence during the hearing counted as evidence against the claim; that argument has been withdrawn because the images did not exist publicly at the time of the hearing, so the silence is explained by timing rather than by the claim's merit.

disputes.bottom_line: None of the individual comparisons in this image set survive scrutiny as identification evidence, in either direction. The 'uncompressed' framing is not demonstrated — a color filter and a stream screenshot are being presented as resolution recovery when neither adds real detail. The different image sets share no common scene, angle, or clothing to compare. And the premise underlying the whole exercise — that clear facial identification is necessary and currently missing — misunderstands the state's own identification methodology, which the case agent has already conceded does not rest on facial clarity from the rooftop footage. This is not evidence that Robinson is wrongly identified; it is evidence that a set of unsourced, uncorroborated comparison images does not meaningfully move that question in either direction. One addition from later material (item 7): a more specific, technically plausible claim about horizontal compression distorting apparent build in parking-garage footage was released after the preliminary hearing concluded, which means it has never been tested by cross-examination and should be treated as a genuinely open question rather than one the adversarial process already addressed. This app initially reasoned that the defence's silence on this point during the hearing counted against the claim; that reasoning has been withdrawn as a timing error, preserved here so it is not repeated.
disputes.next_step: If a specific claim about Twiggs's location during the shooting window matters, the actual testable record already exists: the Discord/text evidence (Exhibit 16) documents his communications with Robinson beginning the evening of September 10, and his own recorded interview statement says he had no advance knowledge. Any image-based claim about his presence at the scene would need to be checked against that record and against a sourced, unaltered original file — not a re-shared comparison graphic with no provenance.

contradictions.title: N1098L's location — RESOLVED by re-extracting its full trace

side_a.source: This app's earlier summary-only extraction
side_a.claim: N1098L (Bombardier Global 6000/6500, Lasai Aviation II LLC) shows 832 Utah trace points, with its last Utah position at ~1:06 PM MDT over south-central Utah — after the shooting.

side_b.source: CharlieFiles.com, citing an aviation-OSINT analyst
side_b.claim: N1098L flew a routine El Paso → Kalispell, MT training run, arriving ~10:38 AM MDT — not over Utah at 12:23 PM.

contradictions.why_it_matters: Both prior claims were partially right and partially wrong. The full re-extracted trace shows N1098L flew a much longer multi-leg day: overnight near El Paso, TX, then a morning transit of Utah northbound (~9:00-9:19 AM MDT, descending to ~4,800 ft near the Wasatch corridor before climbing back to cruise — a terrain transit, not a landing), continuing to Kalispell, MT where it actually landed at ~11:27 AM MDT (not ~10:38 AM as claimed), departing again by noon, then flying south — placing it over SOUTHEASTERN IDAHO, not Utah, at 30,000 ft at the moment closest to the shooting (12:22 PM MDT). It re-entered Utah airspace afterward on a southbound leg around 1:00 PM MDT at 26,600 ft, continuing on to New Mexico, Phoenix, and California by evening. So CharlieFiles' bottom-line conclusion — not over Utah at the moment of the shooting — is correct, even though its Kalispell-landing-time detail was off by nearly an hour. This app's own earlier 'provo_pts: 123' figure reflected two brief high-altitude transits of the Provo corridor, not a landing or extended presence.
contradictions.status: RESOLVED — full trace re-extracted 2026-08-12, see Flight Data tab

contradictions.title: Three different characterizations of Kirk's private Israel message

side_a.source: Charlie Kirk (private, September 8, 2025)
side_a.claim: Wrote 'Just lost another huge Jewish donor. $2 million a year because we won't cancel Tucker' and 'Jewish donors play into all the stereotypes,' concluding he felt bullied by donor pressure and had 'no choice but to leave the pro-Israel cause.' The donor pressure was specifically over Kirk's refusal to disinvite Tucker Carlson from AmericaFest; separate reporting (New York Times) names Zionist tech investor Robert Shillman as having pulled a $2 million pledge over an earlier Carlson TPUSA appearance.

side_b.source: Josh Hammer (public, after the fact — despite having read the same message)
side_b.claim: Called the idea that Kirk was 'turning' on Israel an 'egregious lie,' characterizing it as Kirk merely 'blowing off steam.'

contradictions.why_it_matters: Hammer was in the same chat and had direct access to Kirk's actual language, then publicly offered a categorically cleaner characterization than the private record supports. Andrew Kolvet's public characterization — that Kirk's Israel position had become 'complicated and nuanced' — sits between the two and is closer to the primary document. Three people, three different public accounts of one private message. This message's authenticity is no longer a matter of characterisation alone: TPUSA spokesman Andrew Kolvet has confirmed it directly, on the record, saying 'It is authentic,' and stated he had not shared the screenshot earlier because it was a private exchange. Kolvet also disclosed that he shared the messages with government officials within 33 hours of Kirk's death 'to ensure thorough investigation,' and characterised Kirk's actual position as wanting the Gaza war to end while still supporting Israel — consistent with Hammer's 'blowing off steam' framing rather than a reversal, and closer to the primary text than either public characterisation alone.
contradictions.status: The underlying message is verified AND independently authenticated by TPUSA's own spokesman; the characterizations of what it means genuinely still conflict

side_a.source: Gary Melton, initially
side_a.claim: Presented the September 9 photograph as 'proof she was with her kids at 8:33am PT.'

side_b.source: Gary Melton, after the photo's problems were exposed (children misidentified, wrong date)
side_b.claim: 'The fact is we don't know. It hasn't been clarified by Erika, but it doesn't matter' — while maintaining the photo was still evidence against the Fort Huachuca claim.

contradictions.title: No spent shell casing at the firing position, and no identifying features in the rooftop footage

side_a.source: Popular understanding of the rooftop evidence; prosecution's overall characterization of the forensic case as overwhelming
side_a.claim: The Losee Center roof is established as the firing position, supported by a prone-position impression in the gravel, a shoe impression, and surveillance footage of a figure lying down and then running.

side_b.source: Officer Tyler Bagley, sworn preliminary-hearing testimony, under cross-examination by defense attorney Kathryn Nester
side_b.claim: Bagley confirmed he “never recovered a spent shell casing from the roof,” and acknowledged he “could not identify the person's face, clothing or other distinguishing features” in the footage, describing only a “long object” carried by the individual. The spent cartridge was instead recovered from the chamber of the rifle.

contradictions.why_it_matters: RESOLVED IN PART (August 2026). The casing half of this contradiction has a complete mechanical explanation and this app should not have carried it as an anomaly. A bolt-action rifle does not self-eject; the fired case stays in the chamber until the bolt is worked. The recovered rifle held one spent and three unspent rounds, all engraved, so the fired case was accounted for inside the weapon and was never at the firing position to be recovered. Hull's testimony that no casings were found on or near the Losee building is exactly what the mechanism predicts. What remains live in this entry is the separate identification question — that the rooftop footage contains no distinguishing facial features, which Hull conceded, and that no casing therefore exists as an independent forensic link between the position and the weapon. The absence of a casing on the roof is not itself suspicious — a bolt-action rifle retains the spent cartridge until manually cycled, and the chamber recovery is consistent with that. But it removes the single cleanest piece of physical evidence that would tie the roof to the rifle. More significantly: cartridge-case comparison (firing pin impressions, breech-face marks) is generally considered a more reliable individualizing examination than bullet comparison, and the public record centers entirely on the INCONCLUSIVE bullet-to-rifle comparison (see X6). No reviewed source characterizes whether the chamber casing was compared to the rifle or what that comparison found. Combined with Bagley's identification concession, this echoes David Hull's parallel concession about the rooftop footage (see X9).
contradictions.status: Casing element RESOLVED — explained by bolt-action mechanics and the recovered weapon's contents. Identification element remains open.

contradictions.title: The death-penalty aggravator fight: did the bullet endanger the crowd, or fly over it?

side_a.source: Defense motion filed ~August 12, 2026 by Kathy Nester, Michael Burt, Richard Novak, and Staci Visser (41 pages)
side_a.claim: Kirk was Robinson's “only intended target”; only one shot was fired and no one else was struck; “the only evidence presented supports that the bullet traveled above, not through, the crowd”; and prosecutors “failed to establish the aggravating circumstance necessary under the law” — that the shooting knowingly created a great risk of death to a person other than Kirk, the specific statutory aggravator (Utah Code 76-5-202) that makes this a death-penalty-eligible case rather than ordinary aggravated murder.

side_b.source: Prosecution's response, per reporting from KUER and other outlets
side_b.claim: Robinson loaded the rifle with four bullets, not one — evidence, prosecutors argue, that he anticipated he might miss Kirk and accepted the risk of firing again, “thereby putting others in danger.” Prosecutors further argue that numerous people were within a “zone of danger” around Kirk at the time of the shot, where a stray or ricocheting round could have struck a bystander regardless of where the fatal bullet's flight path actually terminated.

contradictions.why_it_matters: This is not a rhetorical dispute; it decides whether Robinson remains eligible for the death penalty. The defense's trajectory claim connects directly to this app's own independent ballistics-geometry analysis (Deep Dives — Wound Ballistics Physics): the hearing-derived figures of an 80 ft elevation and a 10.65-degree downward angle over roughly 142 yards describe a shot fired down onto an elevated stage, which is at least geometrically consistent with a flight path passing above general crowd head-height depending on the stage height and crowd's actual standoff distance — neither of which this app has independently verified. The prosecution's four-bullets argument is a different kind of claim entirely: it infers anticipated risk from magazine loading, not from the actual measured trajectory, and does not by itself rebut the defense's specific 'traveled above the crowd' assertion. Neither side's core factual claim (the bullet's exact vertical clearance over the crowd; what loading four rounds demonstrates about Robinson's state of mind) has been show-cased with hearing testimony from a ballistics or trajectory-reconstruction witness in reporting reviewed for this app.
contradictions.status: Unresolved — pending Judge Tony Graf's ruling on whether the death penalty remains available, argued separately from the September 1, 2026 bindover (probable cause) hearing

contradictions.why_it_matters: Both statements come from the prosecution, and they are not strictly contradictory — the state's explanation, that the gait was caused by a concealed rifle and normalized once the rifle was deployed, is internally coherent and may well be correct. The problem is evidentiary rather than logical. The limp is one of only three physical markers the state has offered for identifying the person in footage that, by the lead investigator's own concession, shows no identifiable face and no visible weapon. That marker is absent at the one moment the identification matters most. The explanation for its absence is itself an inference about an unseen object rather than an observation, and it is circular in structure: the gait proves a concealed rifle, and the concealed rifle explains the gait's disappearance. An independent demonstration cited in fact-check coverage also showed that concealing a rifle in a pants leg makes climbing stairs markedly difficult, while Hull testified the individual ascended exterior stairs to reach the roof.
contradictions.status: Unresolved — not disputed by any party, because no party appears to have placed the two statements side by side

contradictions.title: Egyptian aircraft alongside Air Force One: the escort is real, the presidential jet could not have been there

side_a.source: Video circulating on X, reported to this app as showing Egyptian aircraft beside Air Force One, with a tip that they shared a runway
side_a.claim: Egyptian aircraft were spotted next to Air Force One, suggesting an unremarked or concealed relationship.

side_b.claim: Two separate things are being merged. This is legally permissible — Utah preliminary hearings run on a light burden and admit hearsay — which is precisely why the State's materiality argument worked. contradictions.title: The bullet is engineered against the exact failure the evidence shows

side_a.source: Published design specification and gel performance for the identified load, Remington .30-06 150gr Core-Lokt
side_a.claim: The bullet is built around a mechanical jacket-to-core lock — a tapered jacket with an internal hourglass cavity — whose stated design purpose is preventing jacket-core separation. Published weight retention is 65-80%, against 50-70% for conventional soft points. In 10 percent ordnance gelatin the 150-grain load penetrates approximately 23 inches while expanding to roughly twice diameter, and it is a medium-to-large game round whose users routinely report exits on deer and elk.

side_b.source: ATF recovery and testimony of examiner Samantha Carner
side_b.claim: What was recovered is a jacket separated from its core plus four lead fragments — five pieces — from a neck roughly five to six inches across, with no exit wound. The four lead fragments were unsuitable for comparison, and the single usable jacket fragment produced an inconclusive result, with neither sufficient agreement nor sufficient disagreement to identify or exclude the rifle.

contradictions.why_it_matters: This app previously resolved the no-exit finding by attributing it to bullet design, rating that conclusion supported. That was wrong and has been corrected. The named load is engineered specifically against the behaviour observed, and its designed penetration is roughly four times the width of the structure it allegedly failed to exit. The energy analysis is unaffected and still rules out the most common alternative explanation: at 142-200 yards the round carries 2,000-2,200 ft-lbs, four to seven times what handgun rounds that fail to exit soft tissue carry. A direct cervical-vertebra strike at roughly 2,500 ft/s remains the best single candidate, since expanding bullets can fail catastrophically on bone and gel figures assume soft tissue without it. But the margin is wide, no forensic pathologist has testified to the wound track, and the autopsy is sealed. This does not support any particular alternative theory — several have been separately refuted on their own evidence — it means the terminal ballistics are genuinely unresolved on the public record.
contradictions.status: Open — resolvable only by the sealed autopsy and wound-track testimony at trial

contradictions.title: The four-round aggravator inference versus how a scoped Mauser is actually loaded

side_a.source: Prosecution argument in the death-penalty aggravator dispute, 2026
side_a.claim: Robinson loaded the rifle with four bullets rather than one, which shows he anticipated he might miss Kirk and accepted the risk of firing again, thereby putting others in danger and satisfying the statutory aggravator of knowingly creating a great risk of death to a person other than the victim.

side_b.source: The mechanical characteristics of the weapon, corroborated by ATF exhibit photography
side_b.claim: A Mauser 98 has a five-round internal box magazine and no detachable magazine. A conventionally mounted scope blocks stripper-clip loading entirely, because the clip seats in a guide machined into the rear receiver bridge where a scope base sits. Rounds must therefore be pressed in individually by thumb. Four rounds in a five-round rifle is a stopping point during hand-feeding, not a magazine capacity. Published exhibit photography shows four separately itemised ATF cartridge exhibits, corroborating the count.

contradictions.why_it_matters: The prosecution's inference treats four rounds as a deliberate choice signalling anticipated missing. The mechanical reality is that the rifle was loaded below its own capacity by the only method the weapon permits, one round at a time. That does not refute the aggravator — someone loading four rounds by hand did make four separate decisions — but it removes the implicit comparison to a magazine deliberately filled, and it cuts against reading the number as meaningful in itself. Neither side, on the public record, has addressed how the weapon actually loads, and the argument is currently being conducted as though the round count were self-interpreting.
contradictions.status: Unresolved — pending Judge Graf's ruling on the aggravator; the mechanical point appears unraised by either party
contradictions.app_reference: Deep Dives tab — Scope Placement vs. Bolt-Action Loading; contradiction X36

side_a.claim: 1TEN LLC is reported at 18521 E Queen Creek Rd, Queen Creek, AZ 85142, with no suite or box number, across four consecutive filing years.

contradictions.title: UVU commissioned a public review of the shooting due before summer 2026; no report has appeared

side_a.source: Utah Valley University announcements, September and December 2025
side_a.claim: An independent third-party review of the assassination and the university's security protocols was commissioned, scheduled to begin the first week of January 2026 and conclude in late spring, before summer 2026, with a report prepared for the public. Its stated scope included interviews with university leaders, law enforcement, emergency management staff, employees and students, plus review of video, emergency plans, training records and incident logs.

side_b.source: This app's review of the public record, August 2026
side_b.claim: No published findings from that review have been located, past the stated completion window.

contradictions.why_it_matters: This is the only body in the case tasked with independently adjudicating the security question, and the security failure is the single most firmly established conclusion in this entire app at 96-99% confidence. Its findings bear directly on two logged contradictions: X8 and X30, the dispute between Brian Harpole's account of a specific rooftop-security warning and UVU's position on the threat posture. Those currently sit as a named-individual-versus-institution conflict with no independent arbiter, which is exactly what this review was meant to supply. Context already established: UVU's police chief stated six campus officers worked an event with roughly 3,000 attendees, alongside Kirk's eight-person private detail, and the university subsequently moved to hire eight additional officers and two safety managers against a force of 23. Non-publication may simply reflect delay, and this app has not contacted the university; the absence is logged rather than characterised.

contradictions.title: What Kirk actually wrote about leaving the pro-Israel cause, versus what it became in retelling

side_a.source: Kirk's own private message, September 8, 2025, released by Candace Owens
side_a.claim: Kirk wrote that he felt bullied by donor pressure and had “no choice but to leave the pro-Israel cause.” This is a primary document in his own words, and this app has treated it as established since it was released (see contradiction X3).

side_b.source: The Grayzone, September 12, 2025, citing an unnamed 'Trump insider and longtime friend', amplified by Press TV, Middle East Monitor and Mondoweiss
side_b.claim: That Kirk had refused a funding offer connected to Netanyahu and was “frightened” of reprisal by pro-Israel forces before his death, following a private backlash from Netanyahu's allies.

contradictions.why_it_matters: These are two very different evidentiary objects being merged in circulation. The first is a document: Kirk's own text, quoted directly, about donor bullying and his intention to withdraw from the cause. It is real and this app has never disputed it. The second is an anonymous single-source account, published by an outlet with a declared editorial position and amplified largely by outlets sharing it, asserting fear of reprisal and a refused funding offer — neither of which appears in the primary message. In wider retelling the chain escalates one step further again, into claims that Kirk said he feared being killed if he left. That formulation traces to a dated primary post: Harrison H. Smith of Infowars on August 13, 2025, stating he would not name names but had been told by someone close to Kirk that Kirk thought Israel would kill him if he turned against them. The date is significant and cuts in the claim's favour on one point: it precedes the killing by four weeks and precedes Kirk's own September 8 message by three and a half, so it is not a retrospective construction built from the leaked text. It remains an anonymous relay whose author expressly declines to identify his informant, posted as a quote-tweet inside a factional argument about Kirk declining to debate Nick Fuentes, with no document, recording or on-record account from Kirk's circle produced. The distinction matters because the documented version — a man under heavy donor pressure planning to change his public position — is significant on its own terms and requires no embellishment, while the escalated version supplies a motive narrative the underlying evidence does not carry.
contradictions.status: Documented at the base, attenuating but not fabricated at the top — the primary message stands; the fear-of-reprisal claim rests on one anonymous Grayzone source; the fear-of-being-killed formulation is a dated, pre-assassination anonymous relay by Harrison H. Smith and remains uncorroborated
contradictions.app_reference: Deep Dives tab — Claims Surrounding the Kirks: Sourcing Tiers; contradictions X3 and X4

contradictions.title: Owens says the Panguitch owner confirmed the charge; the owner publicly denies the connection

side_a.source: Candace Owens, public statements on X
side_a.claim: That she has seen the receipt unredacted, that the bill was paid at 9:47 p.m. by credit card, and that she spoke directly with the restaurant's owner, who recovered the charge and spoke with the FBI. Reporting separately indicates restaurant staff contacted the FBI after seeing photographs of Robinson and that agents interviewed the owner and two servers.

side_b.source: Owner Ralph Perkins, public statements
side_b.claim: That there is no connection between his restaurant and the suspect, and that law enforcement cleared the matter. Reporting also indicates the restaurant could not provide full card details or usable security footage, supplying only the last four digits of the payment card.

contradictions.why_it_matters: This is the load-bearing dispute underneath the timeline conflict logged at X13, and this app had only half of it. The 52-minute impossibility between a 9:47 p.m. Panguitch payment and sworn testimony placing Robinson's vehicle at UVU by 12:30 a.m. is arithmetic and does not move. What moves is which side gives way. Earlier revisions here dismissed the sighting as thinly sourced, which was wrong: multiple staff, staff-initiated FBI contact, and a timed transaction are a real evidentiary base. But the named owner publicly contradicts the account attributed to him, and the payment record as described — four digits, no name, no footage — identifies a transaction rather than a diner. The reconciliation that requires nothing else in the record to be false is that staff recognised a resemblance in a face they later saw in saturation coverage. Neither the FBI nor prosecutors have publicly confirmed whether the customer was Robinson, and the owner reports never being told whether the sighting was verified.
contradictions.status: Unresolved — directly conflicting public accounts from named parties, with the underlying identification never publicly confirmed or excluded by investigators

contradictions.title: Kirk's pastor says he was never afraid; Kirk's own message the day before says he was worried about being killed

side_a.source: Pastor Rob McCoy, Fox 11 Los Angeles, night of September 10, 2025
side_a.claim: That Kirk 'had no fear of death', that 'every day he faced death threats from evil, and he was never afraid of that', that he received 'death threats every day, hundreds', and that his heart was secured in Jesus. Asked directly whether Kirk expressed concerns about assassination, McCoy's answer addressed the existence of a security detail and threats rather than any fear on Kirk's part.

side_b.source: Kirk's own message to his security team, September 9, 2025, read publicly by Andrew Wilson
side_b.claim: That in reply to a briefing on the next day's coverage, Kirk asked that the team be reminded they were there for one person's security only, 'because I'm somewhat worried the left is trying to kill me.' A first-person statement of concern about being killed, made roughly 24 hours before he was.

contradictions.why_it_matters: These are the two closest available windows into whether Kirk feared for his life, and they point opposite ways. The reconciliation that requires nobody to be lying is that both are true of different registers: McCoy describes a settled theological posture toward death, which is what a pastor would perceive and what Kirk professed publicly, while the September 9 message is an operational instruction to security expressing situational concern. A man can be unafraid of dying and still tell his detail he thinks someone is trying to kill him. But the distinction matters because McCoy's 'never afraid' has been cited as evidence Kirk perceived no specific threat, and the September 9 message is direct first-person evidence that he did — and that he named a source for it. It also bears on the separate claim, raised from other directions, that Kirk privately feared reprisal over Israel: the one documented statement of fear he made names the political left, not anyone else.
contradictions.status: Reconcilable — most likely describing different registers rather than conflicting facts, but frequently cited as though McCoy's account settles the question of Kirk's perceived threat level, which it does not

contradictions.title: TPUSA gave two mutually exclusive explanations for the SD card removal

side_a.source: Andrew Kolvet, executive producer of The Charlie Kirk Show, on X (September 2025) and with Tucker Carlson
side_a.claim: That the individual who took the cards is a longtime staffer, a loyal man and a dear friend, that he made the right call, and — in Kolvet's own words — that he remains stunned the staffer had the presence of mind to ensure no one stole them. Kolvet has separately said the cards were turned over to the FBI. This is an account of spontaneous individual initiative to prevent theft.

side_b.source: Tyler Bowyer, TPUSA chief operating officer, on X
side_b.claim: That Farnsworth was commanded by police to take down the cameras. This is an account of compliance with a lawful instruction from law enforcement.

contradictions.why_it_matters: These cannot both be true, and the conflict is now internal to TPUSA rather than between TPUSA and its critics — which is what changes the status of this item. Kolvet's formulation does not merely differ from Bowyer's, it actively excludes it: one does not express astonishment at a man's presence of mind for obeying a police order, and praise for initiative is incompatible with a claim of instruction. Kolvet's version is documented in his own words on his own account, so it is not a characterisation by an opponent. Candace Owens, who raised the discrepancy, adds an argument that stands on its own logic irrespective of her record elsewhere in this case: if the motive were preventing theft, removing an SD card worth around fifteen dollars while leaving the camera body on the table is backwards. The evidentiary consequence is unchanged either way — original media left the scene in private hands before investigators took possession, which is what produced Judge Graf's ruling requiring the state to produce original unaltered footage after the defence objected to TPUSA authenticating its own video. What has changed is that the police-direction account, previously the most exculpatory available explanation, is now contradicted from inside the organisation that offered it.
contradictions.status: Upgraded — no longer merely disputed. Two incompatible TPUSA accounts exist, one of them in the speaker's own published words. Still unresolved: no incident report, radio log or officer identification has been produced by anyone, which would settle it in either direction.

contradictions.title: Four published times for the shot — RESOLVED at 12:23:28 by the hearing transcript

side_a.source: UVU official post (Sept 10, same day) and one Fox News route account
side_a.claim: UVU posted that at about 12:10 a shot was fired at the visiting speaker. A Fox News reconstruction of Robinson's path gives 12:20 p.m. for the single shot fired from the Losee Center rooftop.

side_b.source: CBS News and preliminary-hearing coverage (Fox News, East Idaho News)
side_b.claim: CBS reported a single gunshot heard in the quad at 12:23 p.m. The Day 2 preliminary-hearing transcript resolves this definitively: Agent Hull, testifying under oath and reading video timestamps, states that the reported shot was fired at 12:23:28, and that the figure jumped from the roof at 12:24:42.

contradictions.why_it_matters: RESOLVED. The shot was fired at 12:23:28 p.m. UVU's same-day 12:10 was approximate, and the 12:20 and 12:28 figures carried in post-hearing reporting are errors. This app's working figure of 12:23 was correct. The resolution also fixes the two intervals that actually matter and that were previously unanswerable: the figure was on the roof roughly eight and a half minutes before firing, having reached the exterior staircase about 12:15, and 74 seconds elapsed between the shot and leaving the roof. That second number independently strengthens this app's rejection of the second-shooter malfunction hypothesis, which turned on whether an operator clearing a stoppage in two to four seconds would still have had a firing opportunity. It records a further point worth keeping: four values for the most basic fact in the case continued circulating in mainstream reporting after a public transcript had fixed it to the second, and nobody checked.
contradictions.status: Resolved — 12:23:28 p.m., per sworn testimony reading the video timestamp

trends_methodology.title: Why the Israel search-spike cluster is weaker than it looks
trends_methodology.lede: Circulated analyses claim pre-September 10, 2025 Israeli search interest not merely in Charlie Kirk but in names including Tyler Robinson, Lance Twiggs, Brian Harpole, Deirdre Amaro, Hunter Kozak and Robert Bohls, plus locations later connected to the case. Ranked by likelihood, here is what most probably explains that.

explanations.title: Statistical noise plus normalization
explanations.body: Google explicitly warns that low-volume terms can produce random one-off spikes from statistical noise, and says those spikes should not be interpreted as evidence that individual searches actually occurred. Trends is based on a sample, not the entire search database.

explanations.title: The look-elsewhere effect
explanations.body: Investigators began with hundreds of names, places, buildings, doctors, security personnel, law-enforcement officials, judges and aircraft AFTER knowing the case. Search enough combinations of terms × countries × dates and some apparently remarkable pre-event matches will occur by chance. The striking matches get published; the hundreds of terms producing nothing rarely do. This is the single biggest methodological problem with treating the collection as a probability calculation.

explanations.title: The numbers are being misinterpreted
explanations.body: One article says Trends showed '94 searches' for a name and then '100 searches.' That is not what those numbers mean. Google states Explore values are normalized relative-interest scores from 0–100, with 100 representing the peak within that query — not a count of searches. This substantially weakens any argument built on supposed search counts.

explanations.title: Unrelated people with the same names
explanations.body: 'Tyler Robinson' is not necessarily the same Tyler Robinson every time the string appears. Trends records the query string or categorized topic, not the searcher's intended identity. This explanation weakens for highly distinctive combinations — an uncommon full name plus a specific obscure Utah facility.

explanations.title: Geographic attribution is not IP attribution
explanations.body: The public Trends interface reports aggregated geographical interest. It does not provide a list of IP addresses or identify individual searchers. 'Israel' means the Trends geographic bucket — not verified government workstations. Even sites sympathetic to investigating these anomalies acknowledge VPN exits as one possible explanation.

explanations.title: Real but innocent searches
explanations.body: Journalists, cybersecurity researchers, security professionals, political researchers, Israelis connected to American conservative organizations and expatriate Americans can create a surprisingly large relative score for an obscure term. Because Trends divides searches by total search activity in the geographic and time bucket before scaling, a region need not generate the greatest absolute number of searches to look disproportionately prominent.

explanations.title: Automated or irregular search activity
explanations.body: Google acknowledges that automated or otherwise irregular searches can occasionally survive its filtering and appear in Trends — particularly relevant when dozens of obscure terms appear to behave strangely.

explanations.title: Actual pre-event foreknowledge
explanations.body: Possible in principle, but currently unsupported. Not zero probability. If several genuinely unique people with no publicly discoverable pre-September 10 relationship repeatedly appeared from the same geography in reproducible, sufficiently high-volume data, in a meaningful chronological sequence, that would be a legitimate investigative anomaly. The public Trends evidence found so far does not establish that.

trends_methodology.core_distinction: 'Google Trends produced a historical point associated with Israel' is NOT equivalent to 'someone in Israel searched this name before the murder.' Google itself effectively says that distinction matters for obscure queries: low-volume one-off historical spikes can literally be statistical noise rather than actual search behavior.
what_would_change_it: Original CSV exports made BEFORE the controversy, rather than screenshots generated afterward
Repeated exports or API pulls returning essentially the same dates and geographies
A control study running several hundred similarly obscure Utah names unrelated to the shooting, to measure how often Israel/DC/random countries produce historical spikes
Exact quoted query strings rather than broad Google 'Topics'
Evidence that the same terms appear in another independent search dataset
A chronological sequence that makes operational sense — location → security employee → hospital → named physician → suspect — rather than scattered dates
Actual search volumes large enough to overwhelm the statistical-noise problem
Most importantly: subpoenaed or authenticated Google records establishing genuine queries, timestamps and geography. That would be completely different evidence from Google Trends.
trends_methodology.proposed_experiment: Build a master table of every claimed pre-shooting Trends anomaly connected to the case — Israel, Washington DC, Alabama, Utah — and statistically test them against hundreds of matched control names and places. That would establish whether this dataset is genuinely extraordinary or whether Trends routinely produces this kind of apparent 'foreknowledge' when searching backward through obscure terms. Far more probative than arguing from individual screenshots.
